source_references.title: TypeScript Discriminated Unions for Frontend Developers
source_references.author: Matt Pocock
source_references.evidence_scope: Shows that discriminated unions encode mutually exclusive application states and prevent invalid combinations allowed by bags of optional properties.

source_references.title: How to test your types
source_references.author: Matt Pocock
source_references.evidence_scope: Explains executable type tests with Vitest, compile-time helpers, expected errors, and tsd, especially for public library APIs.
source_references.notes: Source metadata and original paraphrase only; code examples are not copied.

source_references.title: An unknown can't always fix an any
source_references.author: Matt Pocock
source_references.evidence_scope: Explains how any disables and spreads loss of checking, why indiscriminate unknown can shift complexity to runtime, and how generics preserve useful relationships.
source_references.notes: Source metadata and original paraphrase only; article code is not copied.

source_references.title: Where To Put Your Types in Application Code
source_references.author: Matt Pocock
source_references.evidence_scope: Recommends colocating single-use types and sharing types at the narrowest scope that actually has multiple consumers.
source_references.notes: Source metadata and original paraphrase only; article content is not copied.

principles.statement: Represent mutually exclusive application states with discriminated unions so invalid combinations fail at compile time.
principles.evidence_note: The authored article contrasts discriminated states with invalid bags of optionals.

signature_moves.statement: Treat a library's exposed types as an API and verify their positive and negative behavior with executable type tests.
signature_moves.evidence_note: The authored guide explicitly recommends type tests for consumed library APIs.

likely_objections.statement: Replacing difficult types with any or indiscriminate unknown can spread uncertainty or move avoidable complexity into runtime code.
likely_objections.evidence_note: The article traces both failure modes and preserves relationships with generics.

anti_patterns.statement: Moving every type to a central file increases distance from its only consumer and creates unnecessary structure.
anti_patterns.evidence_note: The authored guide says single-use types should remain colocated and shared types should move only as far as needed.

context_dependencies: Apply to TypeScript type design, state modeling, library APIs, and code organization.
